RUNX1 occupancy increases sharply after AI-10-49 treatment, indicating a broad redistribution and net gain of RUNX1 binding upon CBFβ-SMMHC inhibition rather than simple loss of occupancy.

Using the supplied RUNX1 ChIP-seq peak calls, DMSO cells had 1,329 RUNX1 peaks and AI-10-49-treated cells had 9,169. After merging both conditions into 9,266 union RUNX1 regions, 7,950 regions were gained in AI-10-49, only 97 were lost, and 1,219 were shared. Among the shared regions, 1,136/1,219 (93.2%) had stronger RUNX1 signal in AI-10-49 than in DMSO, and the summed RUNX1 peak signal increased about 10.6-fold overall.

The gained RUNX1 sites are biased toward promoter-associated chromatin: 3,307 gained regions were promoter-class, and promoter representation was enriched versus shared RUNX1 sites (Fisher OR 1.47, p=1.65e-09). Most gained RUNX1 sites also coincided with H3K27ac-marked chromatin: 6,819/7,950 (85.8%) overlapped an AI-10-49 H3K27ac peak, consistent with redistribution toward active regulatory elements. Representative gained loci included regions near SYTL3, PLAUR, KLF10, GGA1, DIAPH1, and BCL2L14.

Therefore, upon CBFβ-SMMHC inhibition, RUNX1 chromatin occupancy becomes much more widespread and generally stronger, with preferential gain at promoter-proximal, H3K27ac-positive regulatory regions. This supports a model in which AI-10-49 retargets or releases RUNX1 onto an expanded active chromatin landscape. However, from these peak files alone, one cannot determine which gained binding events are functionally causal for the therapeutic response or whether they activate or repress the nearest genes.
